issues.description: The UML/problem specification declares RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as an int and requires constructors to accept attributes in the same types/order as in the UML. However, the solution's RollerCoaster constructor declares the parameter numberOfLoopings as double (and casts it to int inside). This makes the constructor parameter type inconsistent with the UML/problem statement and with the intuitive student implementation (which would expect an int). It may confuse students about the correct constructor signature to implement and causes a mismatch between the intended design and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the RollerCoaster constructor parameter type match the UML (int). Change the solution's constructor signature to public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) and remove the cast. Alternatively, if double was intended, update the UML/problem text to specify numberOfLoopings: double and document the reason for a double parameter.
